assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new class of matter, defined by topology rather than symmetry breaking, with a clear experimental signature: protected edge and surface states. The HgTe quantum-well transport result is a decisive measurement, and the surface-state spectroscopy of Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 opened a door to phenomena that had not been seen before. Lasting impact on materials, spintronics and quantum devices is already evident.
assessment.attribution: The theory-to-experiment chain is reasonably traceable. Kane and Mele proposed the quantum spin Hall effect, Molenkamp's group observed it in HgTe following Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang, and Hasan's group did the first 3D topological insulator spectroscopy. Eugene Mele is a co-originator with Kane, so omitting him is a real cost. Bernevig, Zhang and others are outside the supplied credit, and I cannot resolve that here.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by many groups, with transport and ARPES agreeing. The field is mature and has stayed stable for about 15 years, so recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Mele's omission from a three-person configuration is hard to justify, and the credit may exceed three people.
The priority claims for the 3D topological insulator discovery (Hasan versus other ARPES groups, and the theory side) need careful checking of the historical record.
Whether the quantum anomalous Hall part (a separate candidate) should be recognised alongside this is unclear.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions is an original experimental discovery with very large technological impact, as it underlies read heads, MRAM and magnetic sensors. It is verified, reproducible and applied, and sits close to the 2007 GMR prize in scientific lineage. It meets my criterion that the original experiment counts and humanity benefits.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera independently reported large room-temperature TMR in 1995, which is the original discovery. Yuasa and others demonstrated giant coherent-tunnelling TMR in MgO junctions in 2004, which made the devices practical. Parkin's group did parallel MgO work and is not in the supplied credit, so the fair allocation of the MgO step is uncertain. Julliere's early low-temperature result is also historical precedent.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly confirmed over three decades and in commercial use. Recognition would be late rather than premature.
uncertainties: Priority between the 1995 discovery and the MgO coherent-tunnelling step, and the omission of Parkin from the supplied names.
Whether a committee sees this as sufficiently distinct from the GMR prize.
I have not independently verified the exact dates and the roles of the groups.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: A new instrument that opened the door to seeing molecules and bonds with atomic resolution, which is exactly the sort of tool-driven advance I value. The qPlus sensor gives stable, sub-angstrom-oscillation frequency-modulation AFM, and CO-tip imaging resolved chemical structure and bond order in single molecules. Impact reaches surface science, on-surface synthesis and molecular electronics.
assessment.attribution: Giessibl invented the qPlus sensor and the underlying frequency-modulation force-microscopy physics. Gross, Meyer and colleagues at IBM Zurich demonstrated intramolecular resolution with functionalised tips. That split between invention and application is clean enough for a three-person configuration, but Binnig-Quate-Gerber (AFM) is an upstream Nobel-adjacent lineage, and the CO-tip idea also involves collaborators outside the credit.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced worldwide and used routinely. The interpretation of contrast (Pauli repulsion, tip relaxation) has matured, and the topic has been stable for more than a decade.
uncertainties: Whether the committee regards this as an incremental refinement of AFM and STM, which were already recognised.
The role of other IBM Zurich contributors in the CO-tip method, such as Gross's co-workers, is not covered by the credited names.
I cannot independently verify the details of the ordering of the key steps.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: X-ray free-electron lasers are a genuine invention, an instrument that gives femtosecond, coherent, brilliant X-ray pulses and has opened structural dynamics and single-particle imaging that could not be done before. Impact is broad across physics, chemistry and biology, and the LCLS and European XFEL results confirm the concept.
assessment.attribution: The SASE theory and design lineage (Pellegrini, Kim, and the Hamburg/TESLA work associated with Rossbach) supports a plausible trio. Madey's original FEL, Bonifacio's SASE work and the LCLS construction team are not in the supplied names, which creates a real credit-allocation problem for an invention that was built by large collaborations.
assessment.maturity: The lasers are in operation at several facilities with many verified science results. The invention is mature, though the scientific payoff is still growing.
uncertainties: The decisive credit is spread over more people than three, and the supplied names may miss key originators.
Whether the prize is better aimed at the invention or at the science it enables.
The committee has to weigh accelerator-physics contributions against the physics-discovery criterion.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, with the magic-wavelength trapping proposed by Katori, gives fractional uncertainties near 1e-18. It is a measurement tool that opens the door to relativistic geodesy, tests of fundamental constants and a future redefinition of the second. The importance and the demonstrated precision are both clear.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and built early clocks, and Ye's group pushed it to the precision frontier. Two names make a clean configuration. The single-ion clock and frequency-comb work were already recognised in 2005 and 2012, so priority boundaries matter, but they do not conflict with these two.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by independent labs worldwide. Practical redefinition of the second has not yet happened, so some would say the impact is still maturing.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to wait for the redefinition of the second.
Overlap with earlier prizes on laser spectroscopy, combs and ion clocks.
Contributions from other lattice-clock groups (for example, at NIST and PTB) are not in the credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Nd-Fe-B magnet is the strongest permanent magnet, discovered independently in 1983-84 and now essential for wind turbines, electric vehicles, motors and disk drives. It is an original discovery with enormous societal benefit, and it is the kind of materials invention that benefits humanity directly.
assessment.attribution: Sagawa (Sumitomo) and Croat (General Motors) independently discovered the compound and magnets, so a two-person prize looks natural and well documented. Other contributors, for example in the Nd2Fe14B structure determinations, are outside the credit.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature, used for four decades. Recognition would be very late but stable. Whether it is physics rather than materials engineering is the real question.
uncertainties: Whether the committee sees this as physics or as materials engineering and chemistry.
The relative weight of the two independent discoveries is a matter of the historical record, which I have not verified in detail.
Both discoverers' patent disputes might complicate the narrative.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened an entirely new platform, twistronics, for tunable correlated physics. The theoretical prediction of the magic angle followed by an experimental observation gives a clear discovery narrative.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted the flat bands at the magic angle in 2011, and Jarillo-Herrero's group observed the correlated and superconducting states in 2018. Cao's role as lead author and the contributions of Dean, Young, Yazdani and others are outside the supplied names, so the configuration is potentially unfair to experimental co-leaders.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by several groups, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and the correlated states is still debated. It is a bit early for a full assessment of the lasting impact.
uncertainties: The mechanism of the superconductivity is still unresolved.
Credit allocation to students and other early experimental groups is not captured in the list.
The prize may be premature relative to the maturity of the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetic skyrmions are a new topological spin texture, first seen in the MnSi A-phase by neutron scattering and then directly imaged by Lorentz TEM, and also at surfaces by spin-polarised STM. Direct real-space imaging is the sort of verification I value, and the potential for spintronics is still a promise.
assessment.attribution: Pfleiderer's group did the neutron observation, Tokura's group did the real-space Lorentz microscopy, and Wiesendanger's group did atomic-scale skyrmion lattices. Theoretical credit (Bogdanov and Rossler, among others) is outside the supplied names and arguably essential. A fair configuration is possible but contested.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced widely, but applications such as racetrack memory are not yet realised, and some of the benefit to humanity is still prospective.
uncertainties: Theory priority (Bogdanov and coworkers) sits outside the credited names.
Applications remain unproven.
The three experimental routes are not identical discoveries, so the allocation of originality among them is unclear.
